sentence: This project uses optimal transport theory to build methods that remove noise from measurements of proton-proton collisions and simulate systems across scales.
This project builds computer vision models that connect their predictions directly to training data, so the models are easier to interpret and update.
This project builds a system that lets low-cost robots offload seeing and planning tasks to a nearby computer over a private cellular network.
This project studies how robots can communicate with observers using only their physical motion, modeled as games in which some information is hidden.
This project studies how an enzyme called phospholipase D and a lipid called phosphatidic acid help cells make and release exosomes.
This project builds statistical methods that combine different kinds of omics data to find genetic changes that lead to disease.
This project builds a public resource that models how proteins interact and assesses the phenotypic effects of genetic mutations.
This project holds a conference where researchers share current research ideas in statistics, machine learning and data science.
This project studies how to compare and match curves, surfaces and other shapes, and builds algorithms that work on large datasets.
This project uses genome sequencing to find the genetic changes behind leaf, fruit, seed and flower evolution in a group of flowering plants.
This project studies Type I CRISPR systems and tries to turn them into tools for editing human genomes.
This project tests ways to turn food waste and seashell waste into fertilizer and sea bricks that help plants grow and reduce coastal erosion.
This project rebuilds a software tool that estimates population size, migration rates and divergence times from genetic data, so it can handle whole-genome datasets.
This project builds a curriculum that teaches cybersecurity through block-based programming of robots.
This project builds tools that compare 3D images of tissue from individual molecules up to complex organs, using two kinds of electron microscopy.
This project builds a small chip that uses sound and light to steer the beam in Light Detection and Ranging systems.
